I was thinking the other day what if we moved information at the speed of light, would it help to speed up the computers systems, or would it be wildly impractical?
Would it be possible to have a computer to have fiber optic cables instead of SATA?

You need a storage device that can process and save the data at the same speed.

It's not theoretically impossible I guess but very expensive. My hopes are for the further development of quantum computers.

In terms of data centers, this already happens, but AFAIK only for backbone-type networking. For non-volatile storage like HDDs and SSDs, there is a bottleneck where you can't read or write the data quickly enough for FO interfaces to be useful.

Like others are saying, it's impractical. The reason fiber optic is good for internet is because over large distances electric signals degrade. They degrade less in fiber optic than they do in copper. Over short distances the data transfer rates of copper vs fiber are significantly closer to each other. That's also why ethernet cables use copper. Wikipedia says the fastest ethernet cables can transfer at 100Gbit/s.

It will be possible when cheaper fiber-on-chip technology goes mainstream. As others have said, this is way overkill for spinning plate disks. SSDs and racetrack memories of the future will be able to take advantage of it.
Of course, we are already seeing "disks" that plug directly into the bus, which may eventually invalidate things like SATA in the distant future.

Electrons move at 1% of light speed. At this point in time, it likely wouldn't make much of a difference. At some point in the future, it probably will make sense. (Also data can travel faster than the electrons themselves.) Finally, data transfer is embarrassingly parallel; just add more wires to the cable to increase the bandwidth.

Electron speed is much more of a limiting factor in CPUs. A photon based CPU would be amazing.
